flash.en: STEAMER SS SINGKEP FROM SINGAPORE BERTHS AT SURABAYA WITH FEVERISH CREW; PORT MEDICAL OFFICERS MISDIAGNOSE MILD STRAIN BEFORE VIRUS ERUPTS.

description.id: Pada awal Juli 1918, kapal uap SS *Singkep* milik maskapai pelayaran kolonial KPM merapat di dermaga Tanjung Perak, Surabaya, setelah berlayar dari Singapura dan Penang. Di atas dek kapal, beberapa awak kapal dan penumpang bumiputera mengeluhkan demam mendadak, menggigil kedinginan, dan batuk kering. Otoritas karantina pelabuhan Belanda menganggap remeh gejala tersebut sebagai 'demam biasa' dan mengizinkan seluruh penumpang turun tanpa karantina. Dalam beberapa hari, penyakit yang oleh surat kabar berbahasa Melayu dijuluki 'Flu Spanjool' atau 'Pilek Spanyol' ini merebak dengan cepat di kalangan kuli pelabuhan, menyusup ke perkampungan padat Kalimas, Pabean, dan Pecinan Surabaya.
description.en: In early July 1918, the steamer SS *Singkep* of the colonial Koninklijke Paketvaart-Maatschappij (KPM) line moored at Tanjung Perak harbor in Surabaya, having sailed from Singapore and Penang. Aboard, several crewmen and native deck passengers complained of shivering, sudden fevers, and racking coughs. Colonial harbor medical officers casually dismissed the symptoms as routine catarrh and granted unrestricted landing clearance. Within days, the contagion—dubbed 'Flu Spanjool' or 'Spanish Cold' in local Malay newspapers—raced through dockside coolie quarters, infiltrating the dense alleyways of Kalimas, Pabean, and Surabaya's Chinatown.

description.id: Jaringan kereta api *Staatsspoorwegen* (SS) yang membelah Pulau Jawa dari timur ke barat menjadi vektor penularan paling efektif. Dari stasiun Surabaya Gubeng dan Pasar Turi, ribuan pedagang dan buruh yang telah terpapar kuman menaiki gerbong-gerbong kayu kelas tiga yang padat berdesakan. Dalam tempo kurang dari tiga pekan, laporan kasus demam merebak berurutan di sepanjang stasiun persinggahan: Madiun, Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Purwokerto, hingga akhirnya mencapai ibu kota kolonial Batavia (Jakarta). Kereta api menurunkan virus langsung ke jantung pasar-pasar tradisional di dekat stasiun, tempat para pedagang membagikan kuman kepada para pembeli dari desa-desa sekitarnya.
description.en: The *Staatsspoorwegen* (SS) state railway cutting across the spine of Java from east to west served as the supreme vector of contagion. From Surabaya's Gubeng and Pasar Turi stations, thousands of infected day laborers and traders boarded crowded third-class wooden carriages. Within three weeks, fever clusters flared in sequential lockstep along the junctions: Madiun, Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Purwokerto, terminating at the colonial capital of Batavia (Jakarta). Locomotives deposited the pathogen directly into bustling open-air station bazaars, where village market-goers inhaled the viral aerosol and carried it inland along footpaths to remote rural hamlets.

description.id: Pada Oktober 1918, gelombang kedua yang bermutasi tiba di pelabuhan Tanjung Priok, Batavia. Keganasan klinisnya membuat para dokter Eropa dan bumiputera terperangah. Pasien yang pagi hari masih segar bugar, pada siang hari mulai batuk memuntahkan dahak berdarah, dan sebelum tengah malam wajah mereka telah membiru kelam akibat asfiksia jaringan terminal. Rumah sakit militer di Weltevreden dan rumah sakit pendidikan CBZ (sekarang RSCM) tidak mampu lagi menampung pasien; lorong-lorong dan halaman rumput dipenuhi tandu darurat. Kuli-kuli pelabuhan di Tanjung Priok ambruk di pinggir kanal dan meninggal di tempat, memaksa Dewan Kotapraja Batavia mengerahkan gerobak sampah untuk memunguti mayat dari jalan raya setiap pagi.
description.en: In October 1918, the mutated second wave crashed ashore at Tanjung Priok, Batavia. Its clinical ferocity stunned European and native physicians alike. Patients walking vigorously at dawn were coughing up bright blood by noon, their lips turning a deep plum black before midnight as pulmonary alveoli flooded with hemorrhagic transudate. The military lazaretto at Weltevreden and the CBZ teaching hospital (now RSCM) were overwhelmed within 48 hours; corridors and outdoor lawns were carpeted with emergency bamboo stretchers. Coolies in Tanjung Priok collapsed beside stagnant canal banks and died on the spot, compelling the Batavia municipality to deploy rubbish carts each morning to collect corpses from thoroughfares.

description.id: Bagi masyarakat Jawa pedesaan, kematian massal yang datang begitu cepat dan misterius diidentifikasi sebagai *pagebluk*—wabah kutukan gaib terbesar yang merusak tatanan kosmos. Muncul ungkapan legendaris yang mengerikan: *'Esuk lara, sore mati; sore lara, esuk mati'* (Pagi sakit, sore mati; sore sakit, pagi mati). Di desa-desa Banyumas, Bagelen, dan Kediri, warga meyakini bahwa roh jahat *Lampor* dan *Wewe Gombel* sedang berpatroli menjelang magrib menculik nyawa manusia. Begitu senja tiba, pintu rumah kayu dikunci rapat, dan warga memukul *kentongan* bambu secara bersahut-sahutan sepanjang malam dalam ritual *rontek* untuk mengusir roh maut. Dupa dibakar di setiap sudut gang dan sesaji diletakkan di persimpangan jalan, sementara jenazah tetangga dikubur tergesa-gesa tanpa kain kafan yang layak.
description.en: To rural Javanese villagers, the sudden, inexplicable slaughter was perceived through the cosmological lens of *pagebluk*—a catastrophic rupture in the metaphysical balance of the universe. The chilling proverb spread like wildfire across the archipelago: *'Esuk lara, sore mati; sore lara, esuk mati'* ('Sick in the morning, dead by dusk; sick at dusk, dead by dawn'). Across Banyumas, Bagelen, and Kediri, peasants believed the malevolent spirit host *Lampor* and infant-snatching demons were riding the evening winds to reap souls. At sundown, doors were barred and bamboo slit-drums (*kentongan*) were struck frantically in non-stop *rontek* alarms across adjacent villages to ward off unseen specters. Incense burned at crossroads and offerings were laid at shrines while neighbors were buried hastily without proper shroud cloths.

description.id: Ketika dinas kesehatan kolonial *Burgerlijke Geneeskundige Dienst* (BGD) mengerahkan mantri-mantri cacar keliling ke pelosok desa di Jawa Tengah untuk mendisinfeksi rumah dan mendata pasien, mereka disambut dengan kecurigaan mendalam. Penduduk desa menganggap bau menyengat asam karbol dan pakaian putih petugas kesehatan sebagai pertanda maut. Trauma atas tindakan karantina paksa masa wabah pes membuat warga kerap menyembunyikan anggota keluarga yang sakit di dalam lumbung padi atau melarikan diri ke hutan ketika para mantri mendekat. Sebaliknya, warga mempercayakan keselamatan jiwa mereka kepada dukun desa yang menggelar upacara tolak bala *ruwatan*, membagikan air jimat rajah, dan menempelkan daun sirih pada dahi penderita demam. Perbedaan pandangan ini memperlihatkan jurang pemisah yang lebar antara birokrasi penguasa kolonial dan jiwa rakyat jajahan.
description.en: When the colonial civilian health service (*Burgerlijke Geneeskundige Dienst*) dispatched itinerant native vaccinators (*mantri cacar*) into the rural interior of Central Java equipped with carbolic sprayers and quarantine registers, they encountered deep-seated dread. Rural villagers associated the acrid stench of phenol disinfectants and the white uniforms of sanitary squads not with healing, but with death and forced internment. Memories of the harsh, burning campaigns of the 1911 plague epidemic led peasants to hide cyanotic family members in rice granaries or flee into teak forests whenever government horse carts were spotted. Instead, the peasantry turned to traditional village healers (*dukun*) who staged midnight *ruwatan* purifications, dispensed talismanic holy water, and affixed betel leaves to burning foreheads—a tragic testament to the unbridgeable gulf separating colonial medicine from the indigenous soul.

description.id: Perekonomian Hindia Belanda yang bertumpu pada perkebunan tebu, karet, dan tembakau dihantam kelumpuhan telak. Di kawasan perkebunan tebu raksasa di Pasuruan, Probolinggo, dan Kediri, musim giling tebu 1918 terhenti seketika. Cerobong-cerobong pabrik gula berhenti mengepulkan asap karena ribuan buruh tebang tebu dan operator mesin giling terkapar sakit atau meninggal di barak-barak mereka. Tebu yang siap dipanen mengering dan membusuk di ladang. Di perkebunan tembakau Deli, Sumatra Timur, kuli-kuli kontrak asal Jawa dan Tiongkok meninggal dalam jumlah yang begitu besar sehingga manajemen perkebunan kolonial terpaksa menghentikan produksi dan mengisolasi seluruh kompleks afdeling untuk mencegah pembangkangan buruh.
description.en: The agrarian export machine of the Dutch East Indies—anchored by lucrative sugar cane, rubber, and tobacco plantations—was brought to a dead standstill. Across the immense sugar belt of Pasuruan, Probolinggo, and Kediri, the 1918 harvest campaign collapsed. Factory smokestacks ceased billowing as thousands of cane cutters and steam engine operatives lay dying in squalid estate barracks. Ripe sugar cane withered and spoiled in the fields. In the Deli tobacco estates of East Sumatra, indentured Javanese and Chinese coolies perished in such vast numbers that colonial plantation syndicates declared complete lockdowns of estate divisions, fearful that labor riots would erupt amid the pile of unburied corpses.

description.id: Di distrik Glodok di Batavia serta Kembang Jepun dan Pabean di Surabaya, komunitas Tionghoa menghadapi krisis mortuari yang belum pernah dialami sebelumnya. Budaya pemakaman Tionghoa yang sangat menghormati leluhur menuntut penggunaan peti mati kayu jati yang kokoh dan upacara melayat beberapa hari diiringi musik tambur. Namun ketika puluhan warga meninggal setiap harinya, bengkel-bengkel pembuat peti kehabisan stok kayu jati; papan-papan kayu randu dan pinus bekas peti barang terpaksa digunakan. Organisasi kemasyarakatan modern seperti *Tiong Hoa Hwe Koan* (THHK) dan serikat kematian *Siang Hwee* turun tangan membagikan peti mati gratis kepada keluarga miskin. Pemerintah kolonial mengeluarkan dekrit darurat yang melarang prosesi arak-arakan jenazah di jalan raya dan memerintahkan penguburan dalam tempo dua belas jam, memicu kesedihan mendalam di kalangan keluarga duka.
description.en: In the sprawling Chinese commercial quarters of Glodok in Batavia and Kembang Jepun in Surabaya, the second wave precipitated an acute cultural and logistical crisis. Traditional filial piety and mortuary rites demanded heavy, sealed teakwood caskets (*guan*) and prolonged home wakes accompanied by solemn percussion ensembles. Within two weeks of the October outbreak, funeral carpenters exhausted their entire supply of cured teak; undertakers were reduced to hammering together rough shipping crates and soft kapok boards to contain the dead. Modern civic associations like the *Tiong Hoa Hwe Koan* (THHK) and mutual-aid burial fraternities (*Siang Hwee*) mobilized emergency funds to distribute free coffins to indigent families. Colonial authorities issued draconian decrees limiting wake ceremonies to twelve hours and banning all street brass bands, forcing heartbroken families to rush ancestors into limestone graves in haste.

description.id: Di tengah krisis yang memuncak, ketimpangan rasial sistem kolonial tampak sangat mencolok. Banyak dokter Belanda dan pejabat pemerintah kolonial memilih menyelamatkan diri ke vila-vila sejuk di pegunungan Malabar, Bandung, atau Tretes. Beban terberat penanganan wabah jatuh ke pundak para 'Dokter Djawa' lulusan STOVIA di Batavia dan NIAS di Surabaya. Tokoh-tokoh seperti Dr. Tjipto Mangoenkoesoemo, Dr. Soetomo, dan rekan-rekan dokter bumiputera lainnya menunggang kuda atau berjalan kaki menembus hutan untuk mencapai desa-desa terpencil. Berbekal obat yang sangat terbatas dan tanpa masker pelindung yang memadai, banyak mantri kesehatan dan dokter muda bumiputera yang gugur terinfeksi di samping pasien yang mereka rawat.
description.en: Amid the unfolding tragedy, the racial fissures of the colonial caste system became glaringly evident. Many Dutch European doctors and senior civil servants retreated to cool, secluded mountain sanctuaries in Malabar, Bandung, or Tretes. The crushing burden of the crisis fell squarely upon the shoulders of indigenous 'Dokter Djawa' graduated from STOVIA in Batavia and NIAS in Surabaya. Luminaries like Dr. Tjipto Mangoenkoesoemo, Dr. Soetomo, and scores of young native doctors traveled on horseback and on foot into the deep interior, entering disease-ridden huts where European officers feared to tread. Armed with meager tinctures and unprotected by gauze masks, numerous young native physicians and rural dressers succumbed to the fatal virus beside their patients.

description.id: Ketika dinas kesehatan kolonial gagal menyediakan obat-obatan modern, kearifan lokal etnomedisin Nusantara menjadi penyelamat hidup jutaan orang. Di setiap pekarangan rumah, para ibu memetik rimpang temulawak (*Curcuma xanthorrhiza*), jahe merah, kencur, kunyit, dan daun meniran untuk direbus menjadi jamu penghangat tubuh. Minyak kayu putih dioleskan di dada penderita untuk melegakan pernapasan yang sesak, sementara daun sirih direbus untuk berkumur guna mencegah infeksi tenggorokan. Meskipun jamu tidak dapat membunuh virus influenza secara langsung, sifat anti-inflamasi dan antioksidan kuat dari kurkuminoid dan minyak atsiri rimpang lokal membantu meredakan badai sitokin dan mencegah infeksi bakteri sekunder, menyelamatkan ribuan nyawa dari maut.
description.en: When the colonial state failed to dispense pharmaceutical remedies, the ancestral ethnobotanical wisdom of the archipelago served as a lifeline for millions. In village courtyards, mothers harvested wild rhizomes of *temulawak* (Java ginger), red ginger, galangal, turmeric, and phyllanthus herbs, boiling them into pungent, restorative tonics (*jamu*). Pungent cajuput oil (*minyak kayu putih*) was massaged onto feverish chests to ease constricted breathing, while astringent betel leaf infusions were gargled to cleanse purulent throats. While traditional herbal formulations could not neutralize the RNA virus itself, the potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties of curcuminoids and essential oils softened the cytokine storm, pulling countless villagers back from the brink.

title.en: The Tragedy of Bali: The Collapse of the Sacred Ngaben Rites

flash.en: OVER 20,000 BALINESE DIE IN WEEKS; SACRED NGABEN CREMATIONS COLLAPSE, COMPELING VILLAGERS TO BURY BODIES IN TEMPORARY COMMUNAUL TRENCHES.

clinicalTarget.en: Balinese traditional banjar villagers across Gianyar, Klungkung, and Badung

description.id: Dari Jawa Timur, virus melompat menyeberangi Selat Bali melalui perahu-perahu tradisional nelayan. Di Pulau Dewata, dampak wabah menghancurkan struktur spiritual masyarakat adat. Dalam tempo dua bulan, lebih dari 20.000 warga Bali meninggal dunia. Di desa-desa adat (*banjar*) di Klungkung dan Gianyar, ritual suci pembakaran jenazah *Ngaben* tidak mungkin lagi dilaksanakan karena kelangkaan kayu cendana, minyak kelapa, dan ketidakmampuan para pendeta menyucikan ratusan jenazah yang datang bersamaan. Para tetua adat dengan berat hati terpaksa melanggar tradisi luhur mereka: jenazah-jenazah hanya dikuburkan sementara secara massal di area pemakaman desa (*setra*), dengan janji bahwa upacara pembakaran roh akan diselenggarakan bertahun-tahun kemudian ketika wabah telah berlalu.
description.en: From eastern Java, the virus leaped across the narrow Bali Strait aboard traditional outrigger perahus. On the Island of the Gods, the pandemic shattered the delicate spiritual equilibrium of traditional communities. Within eight weeks, over 20,000 Balinese perished. In customary village *banjars* across Klungkung, Gianyar, and Badung, the sacred cremation rituals of *Ngaben* completely broke down due to the sheer volume of dead and the depletion of ceremonial wood, coconut oil, and holy water. Grieving priests and village elders were forced to make a profound spiritual compromise: corpses were buried hastily in mass communal graves within village *setra* (cemeteries), with sacred vows that bones would be exhumed for proper purification once the wrath of the unseen powers subsided.

clinicalTarget.en: Sasak farming families, destitute spinners, and malnourished infants in Lombok

description.id: Jika Jawa menderita akibat kepadatan penduduknya, Pulau Lombok dihantam oleh bencana ganda yang mengubah pulau itu menjadi ladang pembantaian. Musim kemarau panjang tahun 1918 menyebabkan sawah-sawah tadah hujan di Lombok Tengah dan Lombok Timur retak-retak dan gagal panen total. Beras langka dan harganya melambung tinggi di luar jangkauan rakyat suku Sasak, yang terpaksa memakan umbi-umbian liar beracun seperti gadung. Ketika virus influenza masuk melalui pelabuhan Ampenan pada awal November 1918, virus mendapati populasi yang sudah berada di ambang kelaparan. Di beberapa distrik, angka kematian mencapai lebih dari sepuluh persen dari total populasi. Kuburan-kuburan desa kehabisan liang lahat; warga yang selamat terlalu lemah untuk menggali tanah keras yang kering, sehingga banyak jenazah hanya ditutup daun pisang dan ditimbun pasir di dasar sungai-sungai yang mengering.
description.en: While Java suffered from extreme demographic density, the island of Lombok was laid waste by a terrifying compound disaster. An unrelenting drought throughout 1918 parched the rainfed paddies of Central and East Lombok, inducing total harvest failure. Grain prices skyrocketed beyond the reach of the Sasak peasantry, who were forced to subsist on toxic wild yams (*gadung*) and tree bark. When the virulent second wave landed at the port of Ampenan in early November 1918, it swept through a population already biologically spent. In certain remote districts, mortality exceeded ten percent of the census. Village burial grounds overflowed; surviving elders were too weak from hunger to dig the rock-hard sunbaked earth, leaving corpses wrapped in withered banana leaves to be hastily interred in the dry gravel beds of desiccated rivers.

description.id: Dinas Kesehatan Sipil Hindia Belanda (*Burgerlijke Geneeskundige Dienst* / BGD) yang dipimpin oleh Dr. W.Th. de Vogel terbukti lumpuh total menghadapi pandemi. BGD beroperasi dengan anggaran kesehatan yang sangat minim—kurang dari 2% dari total anggaran belanja kolonial. Ketika jutaan warga telah terinfeksi, pemerintah kolonial di Batavia baru mencetak pamflet-pamflet peringatan berbahasa Melayu dan Jawa beraksara Hanacaraka yang berisi nasihat dasar: jangan meludah di lantai, tidur dengan ventilasi cukup, dan memakai masker kain. Namun pamflet-pamflet tersebut tiba di desa-desa berbulan-bulan terlambat, ketika sebagian besar penduduk desa yang buta huruf telah meninggal dunia. Kegagalan BGD ini menjadi skandal besar yang disorot tajam dalam sidang-sidang parlemen Dewan Rakyat (*Volksraad*).
description.en: The Dutch colonial Civil Health Service (*Burgerlijke Geneeskundige Dienst* / BGD), presided over by Dr. W.Th. de Vogel, proved utterly paralyzed before the onslaught. Operating on a shoestring budget that represented less than two percent of total colonial expenditures, the BGD had no contingency reserves. Only after millions had already fallen sick did the Batavia administration scramble to print educational circulars in Malay and Javanese Hanacaraka script, advising peasants not to spit on dirt floors, to open bamboo shutters, and to cover mouths with cotton cloth. But these pamphlets arrived months too late in illiterate hamlets where entire families had already perished, igniting scathing condemnation in the newly formed colonial parliament (*Volksraad*).

title.id: Rintangan Kayu Ulin Suku Dayak di Rimba Borneo: Blokade Sungai & Isolasi Mandiri Adat
title.en: The Dayak Ironwood River Blockades: Indigenous River Closures & Forest Quarantine in Borneo

flash.id: KERAJINAN HUKUM ADAT DAYAK MENEBANG POHON ULIN MERINTANGI ALIRAN SUNGAI DI PEDALAMAN KALIMANTAN MENYELAMATKAN RUMAH BETANG DARI KEMATIAN MASSAL PESISIR.
flash.en: INDIGENOUS DAYAK COMMUNITIES FELL GIANT IRONWOOD TREES TO BLOCK BORNEO RIVERS, ENFORCING TOTAL QUARANTINE THAT SAVES INTERIOR LONGHOUSES.

mutationType.en: Exceptional Success of Customary Adat River Closures and Longhouse Isolation

threatLevel.en: Successful Defense (Sharp Divergence from Catastrophic Coastal Port Losses)

clinicalTarget.en: Dayak longhouse communities of the deep interior Bornean river systems

description.id: Di tengah kabar mengerikan tentang ribuan kematian di kota-kota pelabuhan pesisir seperti Banjarmasin, Samarinda, dan Pontianak, para tetua suku Dayak di pedalaman Kalimantan mengambil tindakan tegas berbasis hukum adat. Mengetahui bahwa penyakit mematikan merambat melalui kapal-kapal pedagang yang menyusuri Sungai Barito dan Sungai Kapuas, kepala-kepala suku memerintahkan penebangan pohon-pohon kayu ulin (*Eusideroxylon zwageri*) raksasa untuk melintangi aliran sungai. Di atas rintangan kayu besi tersebut, mereka menancapkan tombak-tombak kayu bertanda kain merah sebagai peringatan adat: siapa pun perahu dari hilir yang mencoba menerobos akan dihujani anak sumpit beracun. Komunitas suku mengisolasi diri di dalam rumah-rumah betang (panjang) mereka di kedalaman hutan belantara, berhasil memutus rantai transmisi dan menyelamatkan peradaban hulu dari kepunahan biologis.
description.en: Amidst terrifying dispatches of thousands dying across coastal river ports like Banjarmasin, Samarinda, and Pontianak, Dayak tribal councils in the deep interior of Borneo enacted swift, radical non-pharmaceutical interventions grounded in ancient customary law (*hukum adat*). Recognizing that the lethal lung sickness traveled via merchant canoes and government launches ascending the Barito and Kapuas rivers, chiefs ordered giant ironwood trees (*kayu ulin*) to be felled directly across narrow gorge channels, sealing off upstream navigation. At these river barriers, carved wooden effigies and spears with red cloth warnings were erected: any downstream craft attempting to breach the blockade faced lethal poison-dart fire from the jungle canopy. By retreating deep into primary rainforests and sealing longhouses, interior Dayak communities severed transmission lines, preserving their lineage while colonial coastal settlements burned through lumber supplies for graves.

clinicalTarget.en: Minangkabau highlanders, interior Dayak river communities, and Ambonese islanders

description.id: Meskipun Pulau Jawa menjadi pusat konsentrasi korban terbesar, pandemi tidak menyisakan Kepulauan Luar (*Buitengewesten*). Kapal-kapal pos KPM yang berlayar secara teratur menyebarkan virus ke pelabuhan-pelabuhan utama: Emmahaven di Padang, Banjarmasin di Kalimantan, Makassar di Sulawesi, hingga ke kepulauan Maluku. Di pedalaman Minangkabau, Sumatra Barat, rumah-rumah gadang berubah menjadi rumah duka; di sepanjang aliran Sungai Barito dan Mahakam di Kalimantan, suku Dayak menutup akses sungai dengan menebang pohon untuk membendung masuknya perahu pembawa kuman. Di pulau-pulau rempah Maluku seperti Banda dan Ambon, wabah menyapu seluruh keluarga pelaut dalam hitungan hari tanpa pernah ada dokter kolonial yang datang menolong.
description.en: While Java bore the numerical brunt of the slaughter, the Outer Islands (*Buitengewesten*) were mercilessly harvested. KPM mail steamers operating scheduled lines seeded the infection into regional maritime ports: Emmahaven in Padang, Banjarmasin on the rivers of Borneo, Makassar in Celebes, and the Spice Islands of the Moluccas. In the Minangkabau highlands of West Sumatra, matrilineal *rumah gadang* longhouses became funerary halls. Along the Barito and Mahakam rivers of Borneo, Dayak chieftains felled colossal ironwood trees across river channels to physically blockade incoming craft carrying the fever. In Banda and Ambon, entire seafaring lineages were wiped out in days without a single European physician ever setting foot ashore.

description.id: Pada awal 1919, ketika daratan rendah pesisir mulai melihat penurunan angka kematian, gelombang ketiga kembali berkobar di dataran tinggi sejuk Priangan, Jawa Barat. Udara dingin pegunungan berkabut di sekitar Bandung, Garut, dan Sukabumi menciptakan kondisi mikroklimat yang memperpanjang daya tahan hidup virus di udara. Ribuan buruh pemetik teh perempuan Sunda di perkebunan teh Malabar dan Pengalengan terkapar sakit demam tinggi di gubuk-gubuk perkebunan mereka. Meskipun tingkat fatalitasnya tidak lagi sehebat amukan Oktober 1918, gelombang ketiga ini tetap merenggut puluhan ribu nyawa tambahan di pelosok Jawa Barat sebelum akhirnya mereda sepenuhnya pada pertengahan 1919.
description.en: In early 1919, as the scorched coastal lowlands finally witnessed a decline in daily burials, a persistent third wave flared across the misty highlands of the Priangan in West Java. The chilly, damp mountain air surrounding Bandung, Garut, and Sukabumi created optimal micro-climates that preserved viral aerosol stability. Thousands of Sundanese women plucking tea on the immense Malabar and Pengalengan estates collapsed with racking fevers in their valley dormitories. While the case fatality rate exhibited gradual biological attenuation compared to the October horror, this third wave nonetheless harvested tens of thousands of additional lives across West Java before extinguishing itself by mid-1919.

title.en: The Voice of 'Oetoesan Hindia': Tjokroaminoto's Indictment of Colonial Apathy

flash.en: INDIGENOUS PAPER 'OETOESAN HINDIA' CONDEMNS COLONIAL DERELICTION; TJOKROAMINOTO LINKS DEADLY DEATH TOLLS TO ECONOMIC EXPLOITATION.

description.id: Pandemi 1918 menjadi titik balik krusial dalam kebangkitan kesadaran politik nasionalis di Hindia Belanda. Melalui surat kabar *Oetoesan Hindia* di Surabaya, pemimpin besar Sarekat Islam, Hadji Oemar Said (H.O.S.) Tjokroaminoto, melancarkan kritik tajam tanpa ampun terhadap pemerintah kolonial. Tjokroaminoto menulis bahwa kematian jutaan rakyat bumiputera bukanlah semata-mata 'takdir Tuhan' atau 'kemarahan roh halus', melainkan akibat langsung dari kemiskinan struktural, kelaparan, dan ketiadaan fasilitas kesehatan yang disediakan oleh penjajah Belanda yang hanya mengeruk kekayaan tanah air. Kritik pedas ini menyulut kesadaran jutaan anggota Sarekat Islam dan organisasi pergerakan lainnya, mengubah duka lara pagebluk menjadi tekad baja untuk menuntut kemerdekaan dan keadilan sosial bagi bangsa Indonesia.
description.en: The 1918 cataclysm proved a seminal watershed in the political radicalization of the Indonesian nationalist movement. Through the influential Malay-language daily *Oetoesan Hindia* in Surabaya, the revered leader of Sarekat Islam, Hadji Oemar Said (H.O.S.) Tjokroaminoto, unleashed a blistering indictment of the colonial order. Tjokroaminoto argued forcefully that the annihilation of millions of native lives was neither an inevitable 'act of God' nor a 'supernatural curse', but the direct consequence of systemic colonial impoverishment, chronic undernourishment, and criminal neglect by a regime that extracted fortunes while denying basic medicine. This impassioned critique resonated across the archipelago, transforming the grief of the *pagebluk* into an unyielding resolve for self-determination.

flash.en: HISTORICAL RESEARCH BY COLIN BROWN REVEALS 1.5 TO 4.37 MILLION CASUALTIES IN INDONESIA; THE GREATEST DEMOGRAPHIC DISASTER IN ARCHIPELAGIC MEMORY.

description.id: Selama beberapa dekade, catatan kolonial Belanda mengecilkan jumlah korban flu 1918 di Hindia Belanda hanya sekitar 400.000 jiwa. Namun penelitian demografi historis modern yang dipelopori oleh sejarawan Colin Brown pada tahun 1987 dan diperdalam oleh para peneliti kontemporer merekonstruksi angka yang jauh lebih mengerikan: antara 1,5 juta hingga 4,37 juta jiwa penduduk Nusantara musnah akibat pandemi ini, dengan Pulau Jawa menanggung beban terbesar lebih dari 3 juta kematian. Angka ini menjadikan Hindia Belanda sebagai wilayah dengan jumlah kematian mutlak tertinggi kedua di seluruh dunia setelah India. Bencana demografis yang terlupakan ini mendesak pemerintah kolonial membentuk Dinas Pemberantasan Penyakit Menular dan memperluas pendidikan kedokteran bumiputera, meninggalkan warisan sejarah yang mendalam bagi sistem kesehatan masyarakat Indonesia modern.
description.en: For decades, conservative Dutch colonial records minimized the 1918 pandemic death toll in the East Indies to a mere 400,000 souls. However, modern historical demographic scholarship—pioneered by historian Colin Brown in 1987 and expanded by contemporary epidemiologists—reconstructed the true, terrifying magnitude of the slaughter: between 1.5 million and an astonishing 4.37 million human beings were obliterated across the archipelago, with the island of Java alone enduring over three million deaths. This establishes colonial Indonesia as having suffered the second-highest absolute mortality burden in the entire world, surpassed only by British India. This colossal, long-neglected demographic catastrophe forced subsequent colonial health restructuring, expanded native medical training, and left an indelible imprint upon modern Indonesian public health memory.
